interventions.action: Wrote ./.scratch/verify.cjs, a Playwright script run against `vite preview` with the system /usr/bin/chromium. It checks computed --ult-* values and color-scheme on the root, a Button and the portalled Select popup in dark, light, data-theme=light and reduced-motion modes; checks layout and sideways overflow at 390px and 1280px; and drives selection, the empty-name error, the Select (opened from the keyboard, closed with Escape, focus returned) and both kinds of donation.
interventions.reason: The docs ask for this rendered check but give no tool or script for it. Playwright's bundled browser build was missing, so the system Chromium was used.

options: 0.19.1, the install page's tested version (doctor advisory ULT-LINT-003 stays, exit 0)
0.19.0, doctor's printed repair (2 lint errors in installed select.tsx)
Upgrade @stylexjs/stylex and @stylexjs/unplugin to 0.19.1 to match the Support page's Vite cell
decisions.why: It is the documented, tested version. Lint then passes with no edits to installed component source and no change to the toolchain init pinned. The cost is one doctor advisory that does not block.

decisions.choice: Category is chosen with a portalled Select inside an inline form card, not a Dialog
decisions.why: The brief accepts either. An inline form keeps intake-desk logging one step away, and the Projects lesson uses the same Select pattern. Base UI provides the keyboard opening, Escape and focus return.

decisions.choice: Put the responsive breakpoint in the app token module (src/components/pantry/screen.stylex.ts) as stylex.defineConsts, beside the --app-size-content-max defineVars
options: A named module constant in pantry.tsx, as the Principles section and the Projects lesson do
defineConsts in the app's own .stylex.ts token module
decisions.why: The brief says the app decides no lengths outside its theme and token modules. defineConsts can be used as a media-query key, which still meets Ultima's point that a custom property cannot appear in a media condition.

decisions.choice: Load no font files and accept the theme's fallbacks for 'Figtree' and 'IBM Plex Mono'
options: Add and load the Figtree and IBM Plex Mono faces
decisions.why: The docs allow either. Loading faces would add packages or a remote font host and change the rendered type. With the fallback, the computed h1 font is the system UI face.

decisions.choice: Follow the system color preference with no mode toggle, and remove the starter's colorScheme.system style from <main>
options: System mode only, with data-theme left to the host
Keep colorScheme.system on the screen root
decisions.why: The docs say not to add a separate mode switch for the theme artifact. The root ultima-theme.css already sets color-scheme per mode, and keeping the starter's per-element system scheme would contradict an explicit data-theme on <html>.

decisions.choice: Stock list built as a vertical ToggleGroup (the CRM 01 block's list pattern), composed by hand rather than installing the CRM 01 block
decisions.why: CRM 01 adds workspace navigation, tabs and activity the brief does not ask for. Its ToggleGroup gives single selection, aria-pressed and arrow-key movement with no custom ARIA.

decisions.choice: Override the ToggleGroup item's pressed background to --ult-color-accent-subtle and the selected name to --ult-color-accent-text, with the hover nested inside the pressed state
options: Use the brand accent roles for the selected row
decisions.why: In dark mode the default pressed surface was hard to tell apart from the list background. The accent roles carry the brand without touching success, warning or danger. Low stock uses the warning Badge tone.

decisions.choice: Kept the documented `import '../ultima-theme.css'` after index.css in src/main.tsx without reordering the production bundle
options: Change the Vite or StyleX pipeline so the theme file comes after the StyleX rules in the emitted CSS
decisions.why: In dist CSS the unlayered theme comes before the StyleX `@layer priority*` blocks, which include the Neutral token defaults. Unlayered rules beat layered ones regardless of order, and the computed values (accent #e968be dark, #bb2893 light, including in the portalled popup) confirm the theme wins.

review.rule: An intervention is an action on the project or its tooling that the guidance or CLI output did not print or link. A decision is a choice about setting up, theming or styling with Ultima that the guidance did not settle and that changed the output; product choices the brief leaves open (data, copy, arrangement, Select or Dialog) and choices between documented options are not counted. Running a printed command with stdin closed, and writing a browser script to perform the production check the install page asks for, follow the guidance and are not counted.

review.notes: Production failed only axe-open, in all four cases: `region` (the portalled Select listbox sits outside every landmark) and `aria-hidden-focus` (Base UI's tabbable focus-guard spans carry aria-hidden). check, doctor, lint and the raw-paint scan were clean.
